speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your examination. I am Dr. Agent; since you are a newborn, I will rely on your parents to describe any symptoms or concerns you have noticed. To begin, has your baby been feeding well, and have you noticed any changes in skin color, breathing patterns, or temperature?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunizations, I need to know if you have noticed any specific physical signs like yellowing of the skin or eyes, or if the baby has developed a rash or blisters since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome

The constellation of a continuous heart murmur (likely a patent ductus arteriosus), blueberry muffin rash (non-blanching purpura), cataracts (cloudy lenses), and sensorineural deafness represents the classic triad of Congenital Rubella Syndrome. Given the history of no prenatal care, this fits the profile of a congenital infection acquired in utero. No further questioning is required to reach this diagnosis.
